rows.description: Parents see missed events and accept the excuses to keep peace, and start accommodating the fear. Kindly encouraging small steps, rather than rescuing every time, helps more than either pushing or shielding.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager asks parents again and again whether everything will be fine and checks the same worry many times. Reassurance eases the fear for a few minutes but teaches the mind it cannot cope alone.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: The person checks repeatedly, rehearses lines, brings a friend everywhere or seeks constant reassurance. Each safety habit brings brief calm but confirms that the situation was dangerous without them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: anger, calm, trust

rows.description: Opportunities are declined, study or work suffers and the person feels ashamed and disappointed in themself. The cost of avoiding now outweighs the cost of the original fear.
graph_context: previous stage: Safety behaviours and what-ifs
next stage: Facing it in small steps
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: disappointment, fear, shame

rows.subtype: Stage 6: Facing it in small steps [Observer]
rows.description: A friend accompanies an anxious person to a class, then sits farther away next time. Gradually reducing the help, while praising the effort, builds the person's own confidence.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Stage 6: Facing it in small steps [Response]
rows.description: The person lists feared situations from mild to hard and tries the easiest, staying until the fear eases. Learning by doing that the feared outcome does not happen is what actually retrains the alarm.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: If anxiety keeps limiting daily life, the person sees a doctor or trained therapist rather than only self-help. Asking early is a sensible step, and friends can help by being patient without taking over.
graph_context: previous stage: Facing it in small steps
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager takes part in rituals and prayers as a normal part of family and community life. Faith is warm, unquestioned and tied to belonging, with few questions asked.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: Science lessons, a tragedy or a contradiction in teachings raises a question about what was always accepted. The teen feels guilt and fear at even asking, and worries about disappointing elders.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: disappointment, fear, anxiety, guilt

rows.description: Away from home, the young adult skips practices, reads widely and meets people of other faiths and none. The old certainty loosens, bringing both freedom and a sense of loss.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
